messages.message:
Patch Set 3:

(2 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Mostly good, a couple of suggestions inline. The core logic is sound: reading the per-device disable_ipv6 knob is the authoritative test, since addrconf_add_dev() consults only idev->cnf.disable_ipv6 and a write to net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6 is propagated into every existing device's copy. The main question is whether an IPv4-only veth is something the suite has to live with, or something it can fix.

commit.subject: LU-20507 tests: don't require IPv6 on the fake interface
commit.message:
LU-20507 tests: don't require IPv6 on the fake interface

setup_fakeif() adds an IPv6 address to the fake interface and
treats a missing address as a fatal error. A node that sets
net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6 gives every new device
disable_ipv6=1, so the add fails and every test that calls
setup_fakeif() fails with "Failed setup test1pg".

A device takes disable_ipv6 from the default when it is
registered, so the interfaces that came up before the setting
was applied still carry an IPv6 address. Read the setting the
veth itself was given and only require the IPv6 address where
the interface accepts one. A namespace veth starts from the
kernel defaults and keeps its address.

FAKE_NID is the IPv6 address when FORCE_LARGE_NID is set, and
the ip2nets rules in test_160 match the fake interface on that
address. Neither can run when the veth refuses IPv6, so skip
in these two cases.

Record intf_has_ipv6 ${INTERFACES[0]} in HAVE_IPV6 rather than
repeat it in each caller.

Fixes: d3d332577537 ("LU-17989 tests: Cleanup fake interface usage")
Test-Parameters: trivial
Signed-off-by: Chris Horn <chorn@ddn.com>
Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5
